title: The returns behind four-party grant relationships
question: Which filer reported each leg of a four-organization circuit or two parallel routes?
finding: 5 circuits and 114 two-route origin/destination pairs have matching reporting dates. Each group below links to all four reported grants.
how: In the two-route test, group by original payer and final recipient within a period. If more than two intermediaries qualify, show the two lowest EINs. The circuit numbers group related rows and have no monetary meaning.
limits: These are grant structures and reporting gaps. Their occurrence does not establish the order of payments, a hidden beneficiary or an improper use of City funds. Inspect the underlying project agreements and bank or ledger dates. Examples identify the first filer’s archived return. Schedule I, Part II requires an itemized recipient entry when a domestic organization or government receives more than $5,000 in total grants or assistance from the filer during the tax year. Smaller grants may be absent. Under the IRS instructions, an accrual-basis filer following FASB ASC 958 reports the present value of a grant payable in future years. An amount in the cash-grant column therefore does not establish a transfer date.
